reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents OneCoin returns as dependent on selling through an internal exchange and cites a 5,000-euro investment for up to 60 euros in daily profit. It describes repeated account activity, sell orders, transaction values, fees, and a password field, while acknowledging severe selling restrictions and directing viewers toward Bitcoin-mining earnings and recommendations at deutschlandteam.nl. The material does not establish website behavior, completed transactions, realized returns, or user losses.

citations.quote: We recommend selling OneCoins.
I want to show you today, how you can get 1coins back to euros. This is the sale of 1coins.
Tycoons, who put up an investment of 5,000 euros on the coin, can sell a maximum profit of 60 euros per day at a rate order is set.
Log in daily and do the selling until you have returned to it.
we have decided to exit the OneCoins... and instead earn from Bitcoin mining.

opening.argument: The presentation repeatedly qualifies the opportunity instead of offering an unconditional promise. It expressly says there is no free trade, that buying is extremely limited, and that selling opportunities are severely restricted. It even reports that the restrictions were contrary to announcements and ultimately says the team decided to leave OneCoin. Those warnings are difficult to reconcile with a deceptive guarantee of easy returns. The reference to possible proceeds is framed within account limits and operational conditions, not as a certain outcome for viewers.

citations.quote: but there is still no free trade for this platform.
Unfortunately, the option of buying is extremely limited
we have decided to exit the OneCoins... and instead earn from Bitcoin mining.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side treats the discussion of a 5,000-euro investment and daily profit as if it were a promise. But the same material emphasizes severe limits and says the team exited OneCoin because of them. “Log in daily” describes a process, not a guaranteed return, and the cited website is presented for recommendations after the stated move toward Bitcoin mining.

citations.quote: Tycoons, who put up an investment of 5,000 euros on the coin, can sell a maximum profit of 60 euros per day at a rate order is set.
Since even this internal stock market... has extreme restrictions
we have decided to exit the OneCoins... and instead earn from Bitcoin mining.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Warnings about restrictions do not eliminate the central financial inducement. The presentation still links an investment to a stated daily profit and instructs viewers to keep selling until they recover their money. Leaving OneCoin for another earning recommendation does not make the original return claim merely cautionary.

citations.quote: Tycoons, who put up an investment of 5,000 euros on the coin, can sell a maximum profit of 60 euros per day at a rate order is set.
Log in daily and do the selling until you have returned to it.

opening.argument: This is most naturally read as an operational demonstration of how the internal exchange worked. The speaker introduces the purpose as showing viewers how to get OneCoins back to euros, then explains where to click, how to place an order, and how account limits affect the transaction. The frames reinforce that instructional format by displaying an exchange interface and a sell-order screen. Explaining a constrained workflow, including its limitations, is different from certifying that the system will produce profits.

citations.quote: I want to show you today, how you can get 1coins back to euros.
So if you want to sell, then go to Exchange in the backoffice you click first on exchange and in trading for example.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The presence of instructions does not turn the video into neutral education. The title and narration center on selling OneCoins, explain how to recover euros, describe price increases, and direct viewers to a recommendation site. A tutorial can still be promotional when its lesson is how to obtain returns from the promoted token.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the material a demonstration does not answer what it demonstrates: selling a token for euros and recovering an investment. The step-by-step interface guidance operationalizes the claimed return mechanism, while the stated account tiers connect investment size with possible profit. Educational format and financial promotion can coexist.

citations.quote: Tycoons, who put up an investment of 5,000 euros on the coin, can sell a maximum profit of 60 euros per day at a rate order is set.
Log in daily and do the selling until you have returned to it.

opening.argument: The observable material describes an ordinary account-based exchange workflow with explicit quantity and value limits, not a demonstrated scam mechanism. It says the internal market has no free trade, limits purchases and sales, and caps the example transaction at 36 euros. The screen shows an order form, but the supplied material does not establish a completed sale, a realized return, or a request for payment credentials. The website is described as offering recommendations, without evidence here of what it does beyond that description.

You can find our recommendations at www.deutschlandteam.nl.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The relevant mechanism is present even without a completed transaction: the narration links OneCoin ownership and investment to selling for euros, specifies account-based limits, and tells viewers to repeat sales until their money is recovered. The absence of a proven completed sale does not erase the promoted purchase-and-appreciation proposition.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A capped exchange screen is still part of the claimed returns mechanism. The material explicitly describes putting up 5,000 euros for up to 60 euros per day and recommends selling OneCoins. Whether a transaction was completed is not necessary to show that the content promotes returns tied to token purchase or holding.
